question: What enables the body to leap rather than remain held back by fear of falling?
premises: The body has an inner impulse toward rising that includes leaping and falling.
The body is made to leap when that impulse is active.
Leaping occurs through the removal of fear of falling to the opposite side.
inference: Action becomes possible when the mind's opposing fear is removed, allowing the body's rising impulse to express itself.
uncertainties: The long compound in the second token can be parsed with slightly different emphasis on 'nature' versus 'desire'.
plain_english: The body leaps because of an inner impulse to rise that naturally includes leaping and falling. It is made to leap when the fear of falling to the opposite side is removed.
